name: Southern Min (Minnan)

ancestors.notes: Min split from the Sinitic mainstream before the Middle Chinese of the rime dictionaries; its colloquial layer is not derivable from Middle Chinese (Norman 1988).
Middle Chinese supplies Minnan's literary reading layer (文讀) alongside the older colloquial layer.

notes: Southern Min (Hokkien/Taiwanese) romanised input contract: Pe̍h-ōe-jī (POJ, Douglas 1873), the oldest and most widely attested Minnan romanisation, inter-convertible with the official Taiwanese Romanization System (Tâi-lô). Consonant digraphs ph/th/kh/ch/chh earn their keys by test 1 (aspiration is not a concatenation of the base stop's IPA plus a letter h has no independent /h/ segment there) and ng by test 2 (one nasal segment). Nasalised finals (ann/inn/enn/onn/unn) earn their keys by test 2: POJ's trailing nn spells nasality of the WHOLE syllable nucleus, one phonological feature, not a coda consonant. Tone (7-8 citation tones, marked by diacritics on the nucleus vowel in POJ) is not yet encoded in this skeleton; Minnan tone is lexical/tonal, exempting it from the stress schema per quality_tiers.md. No WikiPron gold exists in this romanisation (WikiPron's nan_hani files are Han-character keyed, a script mismatch with this spec's romanised input contract), so no benchmark is claimed and the tier stays at skeleton.
